title: Restoration Liaison & Customer Status Orchestration Playbook
author: Ravi Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines the role of the Restoration Liaison, the standardized orchestration for customer-facing status updates during incidents, and the operational patterns for fast, Observable restoration. It consolidates event sequencing, runbook steps for common degradation classes, templated status-page and customer-email content, and a game-day curriculum to validate the flow. Intended audience: SREs, on-call engineers, incident commanders, support leads, and customer success.

Goals and scope:
- Keep customers informed with clear, consistent messages while engineering focuses on restoration.
- Ensure latency and availability incidents follow a predictable handoff model that minimizes duplicated work and prevents noisy updates.
- Provide a single-source runbook matrix for the 6 common incident classes we observe (control-plane, inference-degradation, model-quality regression, capacity-starvation, networking-regions, credentialing).
- Include measurable targets for update cadence, ownership timelines, and escalation windows.

Roles & responsibilities:
1) Incident Commander (IC): coordinates technical remediation, owns the incident timeline, and approves technical detail in status updates.
2) Restoration Liaison (RL): single contact responsible for customer communications (status page, email, customer success updates). RL is not the IC; RL translates technical state into customer-facing language.
3) Primary Resolver: engineers acting on the root cause; owns runbook execution.
4) Support/CX Representative: triages customer tickets and surfaces critical enterprise customers to RL/IC.
5) Communications Lead: for high-severity incidents (>SEV1) works with RL on executive-level messaging.

Incident classification (short):
- LATENCY-DEG: End-user token latency increased above SLO for >5m (SLO: P95 < 300ms).
- THROUGHPUT-STARVE: sustained request queueing and throttling (> 5% request failures).
- MODEL-REGRESSION: automated quality monitors detect generation drift for a tracked prompt-set (>=5 failing prompts).
- CONTROL-PLANE: API auth/route resolution failures or config-store errors.
- REGION-OUTAGE: provider region unavailable or cross-region routing issues.
- SECURITY-INCIDENT: confirmed data-exposure or credential compromise (follow security SOP instead).

Restoration Liaison playbook (step-by-step):
1) Triage & assignment (0-5 minutes): IC declares incident class and severity. IC or SRE rotation assigns RL and posts names in the incident channel and incident doc header.
2) Initial customer-facing message (within 10 minutes for SEV1, 30 minutes for SEV2): RL posts a short status page entry using the template below. Keep the first update concise: impact, scope, and next expected update time.
3) Technical deep-dive & containment (0-30 minutes): Resolvers run targeted runbooks (matrix table below). RL monitors the technical channel and requests plain-language explanations for any new technical findings.
4) Frequent updates (SEV1 every 15 minutes; SEV2 every 30 minutes): RL publishes progress, mitigations, and changed customer impact. IC approves content for SEV1.
5) Mitigation & rollback (varies): If a mitigant is applied (fallback model, routing to spare region, config revert), RL notes the action and expected customer-visible effect.
6) Service restoration announcement (when verification criteria met): RL posts a resolution message with verification steps and a link to the postmortem template.
7) Post-incident follow-up (within 72 hours): IC and RL coordinate a postmortem and customer outreach plan.

Update cadence & approval matrix:
- SEV1: initial 10m, then 15m cadence. IC + Communications Lead review all messages.
- SEV2: initial 30m, then 30m cadence. RL can publish updates without IC approval if message is non-technical.
- SEV3/4: ad-hoc; RL updates only if there is customer impact.

Runbook matrix (quick reference):
Format: Class | First-checks (commands/metrics) | Fast mitigant | Owner
LATENCY-DEG | Check token latencies (metrics: serving.p95_tokens_latency), GPU queue length, batch sizes | Route traffic to fast-path (quantized model) or enable prefix cache | Serving runtime team
THROUGHPUT-STARVE | Check queue_writes/sec, rate limiter logs, capacity-utilization | Increase reserved pool or enable burst autoscaling | Infra capacity oncall
MODEL-REGRESSION | Run eval harness against gold prompt-set; check model version/weights | Failover to previous model version or enable response-filtering | Applied ML / Model-onboarding
CONTROL-PLANE | Inspect config-store health, auth errors (401 spikes), routing-table lookups | Failover to backup control plane or rotate service token | Platform control team
REGION-OUTAGE | Verify BGP and cloud provider incident pages, cross-region latencies | Shift traffic using smart-routing policy to alternate region | SRE/Networking
CREDENTIALS/SECURITY | Check audit logs for key usage; check token issuance | Revoke affected keys, rotate secrets, trigger security playbook | Security (and IC)

Example runbook excerpt: LATENCY-DEG (detailed)
- Symptoms: P95 token latency > 300ms for >5m; elevated GPU queue > 0.8 utilization.
- Immediate checks:
  - kubectl -n serving get pods -l service=redwood-serving -o wide
  - curl -s https://metrics.internal/api/v1/query?query=serving_p95_latency
  - jq '.data.result[] | select(.metric.service=="inference")'
- Fast mitigants (ordered):
  1. Toggle prefix-KV cache on: POST /admin/cache/enable {service: inference} (requires admin token).
  2. Switch route to cached-quantized variant: rollout set variant=cached-quantized --service inference --region us-west-2
  3. If mitigants fail within 10 minutes, implement emergency throttling: increase rate-limiter quota for enterprise tenants while reducing free-tier concurrency.
- Verification: Monitor serving_p95_latency returning below 300ms for 2 consecutive 1-minute windows.

Status-page & customer message templates
- Short update (status page headline):
  - Title: [Incident] Reduced generation throughput in US-West
  - Body: We are investigating increased latency and failed requests for text generation in the US-West region. Impacted customers may see higher wait times and intermittent failures. Our engineers are actively working on mitigation. Next update: in ~15 minutes.
- Detailed technical progress (internal and expanded):
  - Title: [Incident][LATENCY-DEG] Root cause identified: request queueing due to kernel scheduling regression
  - Body: We identified a kernel selection regression introduced in release r2027-02-xx causing increased scheduling latency on P4 nodes. Work underway: rolling back to r2027-02-05 on affected nodes; expected restoration in 20 minutes.
- Customer email template (for enterprise affected customers):
  - Subject: Incident update: Service latency in US-West (ID: RWI-2027-03-01-01)
  - Greeting: Hello <Customer Name>,
  - Short summary: We are investigating increased latency impacting generation in the US-West region. Some requests may time out or experience longer processing.
  - What we are doing: Our engineers are rolling back a recent kernel optimizer to restore normal scheduling; traffic is being routed to alternate capacity while we verify.
  - ETA & next steps: We expect verified restoration within 30 minutes. We will follow up with a full post-incident summary within 72 hours.
  - Contact: Your support lead <name> or support@redwood.ai (for urgent requests call +1-555-0100)

Post-incident verification checklist (before resolution posting):
- Metrics: P95 latency < SLO for three consecutive 1-minute windows.
- Error rate: 5xx < baseline + 0.2% for 10 minutes.
- Canary traffic: 1000 requests validated across 3 regions.
- Customer signals: No new Sev1 tickets opened for the affected customers in 20 minutes.

Postmortem & customer follow-up template (72-hour timeline)
- Title: Postmortem: RWI-YYYY-MM-DD-XX [SEV#]
- Summary (2-3 sentences): Describe customer-visible impact and duration.
- Timeline: Bullet list of key events with timestamps.
- Root cause: Short written statement of root cause.
- Contributing factors: List config, process, and monitoring gaps.
- Immediate mitigations applied: List what we did to restore service.
- Long-term actions (owners and due dates): Table format example:
  - Action | Owner | Due date
  - Add labeled alerts for kernel-schedule-regressions | runtime-team | 2027-03-15
  - Automate prefix-KV warm-up during deploys | infra | 2027-04-01
- Customer outreach plan: Who will notify customers, the message template, and the timeline.

On-call rotation & RL assignment pattern:
- RL is assigned from the Support/CX rotation for incidents with customer impact; for low-severity incidents RL is the on-call SRE.
- Rotation length: 2 weeks for on-call engineers; RL rotation: 1 week to reduce context switching for Support leads.
- Handoff checklist (at rotation change):
  1. Export active incidents and their last status update.
  2. Review outstanding follow-ups and commitments.
  3. Confirm access to status-page editing and customer email templates.

Game-day curriculum (3 exercises):
1) Latency flash (45 minutes): simulate elevated P95, verify RL can produce two concise updates and enact the prefix-cache mitigant. Goal: <8 minutes to publish initial update, prefix-cache mitigant applied in 12 minutes.
2) Region failover (90 minutes): simulate provider region outage and test smart-routing shift plus customer status escalation to enterprise users. Goal: route 95% traffic to alternate region in 20 minutes.
3) Postmortem drill (60 minutes): complete a condensed postmortem for a past real incident with ownership assignments. Goal: produce an initial postmortem draft within 60 minutes.

Monitoring & observability tie-ins:
- Dashboards to watch: "Service Stability Overview" (high-level: SLOs, incident count, active mitigants), "Restoration Actions" (live feed of toggles and rollbacks), and "Customer Impact" (open tickets, customer heartbeats).
- Automated signals that should page the RL: enterprise error spike (>0.5% increase for a monitored enterprise), status-page offline, or failed postmortem publication.

Escalation & exec briefing triggers:
- Trigger an exec briefing if any of the following occur:
  - >2 hours without verified restoration for SEV1.
  - Major financial impact for enterprise customers (>$100k/hour estimated).
  - Data-exposure confirmed.
- Briefing format: 15-minute summary with RL, IC, Head of SRE, Head of Product. Slides should include timeline, impact estimate, mitigations, and next actions.

Retention & governance rules:
- Incident documents and postmortems are published to Confluence within 72 hours and retained for 5 years.
- Sensitive incidents (customer data or security) must be marked confidentiality: restricted and follow Security evidence procedures.

Appendices
A. Status-page edit checklist:
- Verify headline reflects impact, not the presumed cause.
- Include next update ETA.
- Include link to support contact and enterprise escalation path.
B. Quick templates (copyable)
- Status headline: [Investigating] Intermittent generation errors in <region>
- Short internal note: Root cause suspected, mitigation in progress: reverting rollout rYYYY-MM-DD.
C. Example CLI snippets for restorations:
- Rollback example: rclient rollout rollback --service inference --to-version r2027-02-05 --region us-west-2
- Enable mitigation: rclient toggle prefix-cache --enable --service inference
